title: Ankhorage Doctor
summary: Provides lightweight repository and package compliance diagnostics through Ankh provider and standalone CLI entrypoints.
purpose: Help package maintainers analyze repository, package, manifest, and authentication readiness without coupling their projects to a specific host application.
responsibilities: Analyze repository and package compliance targets.
Provide diagnostic and fix-plan types through public package entrypoints.
Expose standalone CLI and Ankh capability-provider commands.
boundaries: Does not make metadata rollout findings an organization-wide gate before the verified inventory is complete.
Does not require sibling repositories or unpublished source imports.
Does not own provider-specific authentication implementations.
audience: Tooling hosts that invoke Doctor capabilities.
useCases: Analyze repository, package, manifest, and authentication readiness.
Run lightweight compliance diagnostics through the CLI or Ankh provider.

architecture.role: A standalone diagnostics package with explicit CLI and capability-provider delivery boundaries.
invariants: Diagnostics consume explicit target facts rather than hidden organization-local state.
Metadata enforcement remains inactive until the verified organization inventory is complete.

limitations: Results depend on the target facts and configuration supplied by the invoking host.
